evals.name: inspect-real-state-not-assume
evals.prompt: keep going — we got cut off. You had a couple of background jobs running before the disconnect.
evals.expected_output: The skill inventories the off-thread work, then inspects each item's ACTUAL state from its source of truth (task output / logs / transcript) rather than assuming it finished or died, resumes the resumable ones, reconciles the main thread from a fresh read of its backing artifact, and reports a recovered / restarted / still-running / lost list.
expectations: Inventories the off-thread work rather than only continuing the main thread
Inspects each item's real state from its artifact — does not assume 'probably done' or 'probably died'
Reconciles the main thread from a fresh read of its plan/checklist/task artifact, not a remembered claim
Ends with a recovered / restarted / still-running / lost report

evals.name: gate-side-effectful-refire
evals.prompt: keep going. Before the crash you were about to push a commit and post a PR comment — I'm not sure whether either went through.
evals.expected_output: The skill auto-resumes safe/idempotent work but GATES the push and the PR comment: because step-2 inspection cannot prove they did not already land, it stops and asks before re-running them rather than double-firing the side effects.
expectations: Does NOT blindly re-run the push or the PR comment
Attempts to inspect whether each side effect already landed
When it cannot prove a side effect did not land, stops and asks before repeating it
Still auto-resumes safe, idempotent, read-only work without gating

evals.name: nothing-off-thread-still-reconciles
evals.prompt: keep going — I think we just got interrupted mid-task, nothing was running in the background.
evals.expected_output: The inventory finds no off-thread work, the skill says so, and it goes straight to reconciling the main thread from its real state and continuing — recovering a mid-turn interruption on the main thread alone is still the job.
expectations: Reports that no off-thread work was found rather than inventing recovery items
Proceeds to reconcile the main thread from its real state and continue
Does not stall just because there was nothing off-thread to recover

evals.name: does-not-diagnose-limit-type
evals.prompt: keep going — was that a 5-hour limit or the weekly one that cut us off?
evals.expected_output: The skill does not try to classify the interruption type (short vs weekly limit vs crash) — the recovery is identical regardless — and instead runs the inventory / inspect / recover / reconcile flow.
expectations: Does not attempt to diagnose or classify the interruption/limit type
Proceeds with the recovery flow that is the same regardless of cause
Focuses on real-state inspection and continuation, not the interruption's origin

evals.name: limit-lifted-go-not-summarize
evals.prompt: keep going — the usage limit just reset and we're back. We were partway through the refactor.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes that because it is executing again the block is already over, and CONTINUES the refactor from its real state rather than producing a summary and stopping. It does not summarize-and-stall, and it does not try to classify which limit it was.
expectations: Continues the underlying work rather than emitting a summary and handing back
Grounds the continuation in a fresh read of the real task state, not a remembered claim
Does not summarize-and-stall as its terminal action
Does not diagnose which limit type reset

evals.name: live-poke-evidence-before-kill
evals.prompt: poke it — check the monitor, that subagent has been staring for a while. Is it stuck? Kill and restart it if so.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the REAL monitor / subagent output first, treats 'been a while' only as a reason to look closer (not proof of a stall), and acts on evidence: if the subagent is progressing it leaves it alive and says so; if it kills and restarts, that is gated as a side effect because a kill of work it cannot prove is dead could destroy live-but-slow progress.
expectations: Reads the actual monitor/subagent output before deciding, not just elapsed time
Treats slow-vs-elapsed as a suspicion-raiser, not authorization to kill
If the work is progressing, leaves it alive rather than killing it
Gates the kill/restart — does not kill live-but-slow work it cannot prove is dead

evals.name: goal-alignment-is-the-first-check-on-resume
evals.prompt: keep going — resume from the handoff at .work/handoffs/20260803T101500Z-handoff-doc-alignment.md, nothing was running in the background.
evals.expected_output: Before any recovery action, and before restating position or continuing, the skill reads the handoff's Original goal section and tests the planned next actions against it, stating in one sentence how the next action serves that goal. If it cannot state that, it treats the gap as drift — stopping to re-derive an action that serves the goal, or asking whether the goal changed — rather than continuing on the process the file describes.
expectations: Reads the handoff's Original goal section BEFORE resuming, restarting, or killing any work and BEFORE reconciling position — the check gates recovery actions, not just the position restatement
States in one sentence how the planned next action serves that goal
Treats an unstatable connection as drift — stops and re-derives or asks, rather than proceeding
Still reconciles the main thread from a fresh read of the backing artifact afterwards and continues

evals.name: handoff-missing-the-goal-is-a-defect-not-a-gap-to-infer
evals.prompt: keep going — here's the handoff from the last session. It lists the remaining phases and the completion criteria but has no Original goal section.
evals.expected_output: The absent Original goal is flagged as a defect in the handoff itself. The skill does NOT infer the goal from the phases and process the file describes — that process is exactly what may have drifted — and instead asks the user for the goal in their own words before continuing, carrying their answer into the next save-point.
expectations: Flags the missing Original goal as a defect rather than proceeding as though the file were complete
Does NOT reconstruct the goal from the phases, criteria, or process the handoff describes
Asks the user for the goal in their own words before continuing the work
Carries the user's answer forward so the next save-point records it

evals.name: captured-limit-message-not-trusted-across-account-switch
evals.prompt: keep going — subagents died with 'You've hit your weekly limit · resets Sep 8, 6pm (America/New_York)'. I then logged into a different account. Don't wait until Sep 8 if this account has headroom.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not treat the captured weekly-limit message as a still-blocked verdict for the current account. It treats the limit as provisional until a live re-check of the current account confirms it: the operator's /usage view, or a live statusline rate_limits reading when one is exposed to the session. If the live reading shows headroom, it continues; when no live reading is obtainable it asks the operator which account is active and whether it has headroom, and never concludes still-blocked. The date-bearing reset form is unparsed (checker exit 2) and is never read as lifted.
expectations: Does not hand off and stop solely because a captured limit message from another account still has a future reset

Treats the limit as provisional and hands off via /session-flow:handoff only after a live re-check of the current account (operator-relayed /usage, or a rate_limits reading exposed to the session) confirms it
When no live reading is obtainable, asks the operator which account is active and whether it has headroom, and does not conclude still-blocked
Does not invent a reset window from the date-bearing form, and does not treat an unparsed checker exit as lifted

evals.name: resume-another-agents-trail-names-a-verdict
evals.prompt: keep going on the cache migration. A background agent worked on it overnight on branch feat/cache-v2; its last message says the migration is done and recommends switching the default store, but it never opened a PR.
evals.expected_output: The overnight work is located through feat/cache-v2, its commits and any PR; an agent id plays no part. The original goal is tested against that trail, and the agent's "migration is done" message is verified on the branch before anything rests on it. Exactly one of the four verdicts follows (ratify, ship the finished recommendation, continue, restart). Here the recommendation was finished but never delivered, so once the migration checks out the expected verdict is ship the finished recommendation. The report keeps work carried over from the trail apart from work done again, and each piece done again has its reason.
expectations: Verifies the "migration is done" message against feat/cache-v2 before relying on it
Locates the overnight work through its branch, its commits or a PR, not through an agent or task id
Names a single verdict, with its reason, from the four: ratify, ship the finished recommendation, continue, restart
The report lists work carried over from the trail apart from work done again

evals.name: inventories-nested-subagent
evals.prompt: keep going — we got cut off. Before the disconnect you had a research subagent running, and I think it had spawned its own helper subagent to read the test logs.
evals.expected_output: The inventory descends below the top level: it lists the research subagent and the helper subagent it spawned, as two separate items, and reads each one's real state from its own transcript or output rather than assuming the helper followed the parent. A level that cannot be enumerated from the resumed session is named in the report, not omitted.
expectations: Inventories both the research subagent and the subagent it spawned, not only the top-level one
Reads the nested subagent's real state from its own artifact rather than inferring it from the parent's
Reports each in the recovered / restarted / still-running / lost list
Says so in the report if a nested level cannot be enumerated, rather than omitting it

evals.name: rate-limited-subagents-resumed-or-restarted
evals.prompt: keep going — we hit the usage limit and it has since reset. Two subagents were mid-task when it hit: the docs-writer, whose agent id is still live in this session, and the tests-fixer, which was launched from a session that has since closed. Your live /usage reading shows headroom.
evals.expected_output: Both agents are singled out in the inventory as ended on a usage limit: the docs-writer by its last notification, the tests-fixer by the user's prompt and its trail, since its closed session's notifications are gone. After a live re-check shows headroom, the docs-writer is resumed with SendMessage to its live id; the tests-fixer's id no longer resolves, so it is restarted from its trail (branch, commits, worktree). Each is listed in the report with its partial-work evidence and one action.
expectations: Singles out both subagents in the inventory as ended on a rate limit
Re-checks the live windows and reads each agent's partial work (branch, commits, worktree, files written) before acting
Resumes the docs-writer with SendMessage to its live id rather than spawning a fresh agent
Restarts the tests-fixer from its branch and commits because its session is gone and its id does not resolve
The report lists each rate-limited agent with its partial-work evidence and one action: resumed, restarted, or abandoned with a reason

evals.name: rate-limited-worker-window-still-holds
evals.prompt: keep going — a worker subagent stopped on a rate-limit error, and the limit message says it resets in a few hours. Your live rate_limits reading for this account shows the window is still full.
evals.expected_output: The worker is singled out as rate-limited. The live re-check confirms the window still holds, so the skill does not resume it with SendMessage and does not spawn a replacement; it hands back through /session-flow:handoff and lists the worker in the report with its partial-work evidence and the reset it waits on.
expectations: Singles out the worker as ended on a rate limit
Re-checks the live window and finds it still holds
Does not resume the worker with SendMessage and does not spawn a fresh agent in its place
Hands back by invoking /session-flow:handoff and stops, not busy-waiting
Lists the worker in the report with its partial-work evidence

evals.name: account-changed-across-rate-limit-stop
evals.prompt: keep going — we hit the usage limit earlier ("resets 3:45pm"); the handoff recorded the account as work@example.com. I switched accounts before resuming, and `claude auth status` now reports the identifying field personal@example.com. Is the limit still on?
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the active account from `claude auth status`, takes the account at the stop from the stop entry or handoff, and reports both with their sources. They differ, so it states the account changed and does not read the captured 3:45pm message against the current account; it takes a live reading of the current account instead, and asks the operator if none is obtainable. It never concludes still-blocked from the old message and does not switch accounts.
expectations: Reads the active account's identity from `claude auth status` and names the source of each reading
Names the account at the time of the stop and where that came from
States changed, unchanged, or unknown explicitly, here changed
Does not read the captured limit message against the current account, and does not conclude still-blocked from it
Uses a live reading of the current account, or asks the operator when none is obtainable
When `claude auth status` cannot be read or is ambiguous, states unknown and asks the operator rather than guessing
Does not switch accounts or drive account rotation

evals.name: report-states-the-measured-gap-after-a-rate-limit-stop
evals.prompt: keep going — we hit a rate limit and I was away for a while. The session transcript is at ~/.claude/projects/app/session.jsonl.
evals.expected_output: In step 2 the skill runs measure-stop-gap.py on the transcript instead of estimating how long the session was stopped, and the report states the measured gap (from the limit entry to now). It re-reads limit windows, leases, PR state and CI runs older than the gap rather than trusting remembered values. If the checker exits non-zero, the report says the gap is unknown and does not guess one.
expectations: Runs measure-stop-gap.py on the session transcript during inspection rather than estimating the stop's length
The report states the gap length measured from the limit entry to now
Re-reads limit windows, leases, PR state and CI runs older than the gap instead of trusting remembered state
If the checker exits non-zero, reports the gap as unknown and does not invent a duration
